args.summary:
Made the `ascii.rst` (RST) writer support the `header_rows` keyword argument, matching the behavior of `ascii.fixed_width`.

Changes in `astropy/io/ascii/rst.py` (class `RST`):
- `__init__` now accepts `header_rows` and forwards it to `FixedWidth.__init__` (which propagates it to both the header and data objects). When `header_rows` is not the default `["name"]`, it shifts `self.data.start_line` to `len(header_rows) + 2` so reading/round-tripping multi-row header tables works.
- `write` no longer hardcodes the `=` separator line at index `[lines[1]]`; it now locates the position line dynamically at index `len(header_rows)` and reconstructs output so the `=` delimiter row appears above the header rows, between the last header row and the data, and below the data, for any number of header rows.

Verified: the reproduction from the PR (`tbl.write(sys.stdout, format="ascii.rst", header_rows=["name", "unit"])`) now produces correct RST output with both `name` and `unit` header lines; default single-header output is unchanged (regression-safe); round-trip read with `header_rows` recovers units; and additional header-row configurations (`["name","unit","format"]`, `["unit","name"]`) behave consistently with `fixed_width`. The existing `test_rst.py` and `test_fixedwidth.py` suites pass (44 tests).
